record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Determine all positive integers g for which there exist chiral maps, equivalently chiral polyhedra, on orientable surfaces of genus g.

evidence.quote: Problem 19 Determine all positive integers g for which there are chiral maps (polyhedra) on orientable surfaces with genus g.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A map on a surface is an embedding of a connected graph (or multigraph) into a closed surface such that each connected component of the complement of the embedded graph (a face) is homeomorphic to an open disk. An automorphism of the map is a permutation of its flags (incident vertex–edge–face triples) induced by a self-homeomorphism of the surface preserving the embedded graph. The automorphism group of a map on an orientable surface acts semi-regularly on the set of flags; the map is called orientably regular if its orientation-preserving automorphism group acts transitively (hence regularly) on the set of arcs (directed edges). Such a map is called reflexible if it additionally admits an orientation-reversing automorphism, and chiral if it does not (so the map and its mirror image are distinct but isomorphic as abstract structures, with two orbits of flags under the full automorphism group). Equivalently, a chiral polyhedron in this combinatorial sense is a chiral orientably regular map.

Determine the set of all positive integers g such that there exists a chiral map on the closed orientable surface of genus g.
artifact.status_search_result: The complete characterization of genera supporting chiral maps remains open. Partial results are known: Garbe (1969) showed there are no chiral maps for genus 2–6; Conder and Dobcsányi (2001) enumerated chiral maps for genus 7–15; and Conder has extended computational classifications up to genus 301. Infinitely many gaps in the genus spectrum of chiral maps are known to exist, but a full description of which positive integers g arise is not available.

status_evidence.title: Regular maps with simple underlying graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Garbe (1969) showed no chiral maps exist on orientable surfaces of genus 2–6; Conder and Dobcsányi (2001) determined all chiral regular maps on orientable surfaces of genus 7 to 15.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial enumerations by genus exist for chiral maps.

status_evidence.title: Constructions for chiral polytopes (Conder)
status_evidence.snippet: Conder maintains lists of regular and chiral orientable maps by genus; gaps in the genus spectrum are known.
status_evidence.claim: Classification of genera supporting chiral maps is approached only via computational enumeration.
